habits.boundary_condition: If the search is explicitly framed as relatively cheap or budget-focused, keep a quality floor rather than choosing purely by price, with about 3.5 stars as the minimum supported fallback.
habits.condition: When searching for hotels and the user asks for a nice, upscale, resort-style, or highly rated stay.
habits.default_action: Filter or rank hotels starting at 4 stars or higher, and prefer 4.5-star options if they also satisfy the other constraints.
habits.exception_condition: If the user states a different rating threshold, prioritizes cheapest possible regardless of quality, or the rating metric is ambiguous between hotel class and customer reviews, follow or confirm the explicit metric before applying this default.
habits.name: hotel_quality_floor_with_budget_fallback
habits.preference_value: Default to at least a 4-star hotel quality signal, using the metric provided in context (hotel class, Google rating, or customer rating); treat 4.5 stars as an ideal upgrade when available. For explicitly cheap hotel searches, allow a lower floor around 3.5 customer stars while still requiring good reviews.
habits.rationale: Across the cited hotel searches, the user repeatedly balances price with a reusable quality floor: nice/upscale stays are tied to 4-star minimums and 4.5-star preference, while a cheap-hotel case still requires high ratings with a 3.5-star floor.

source_evidence.contribution: Supports the default 4-star quality floor for nice hotels and the 4.5-star ideal upgrade.
